sources.articleTitle: Kaduna-Kano rail line to be inaugurated 3 December – APC Campaign Council
Jigawa APC inaugurates 2027 campaign council, rallies support for Tinubu, Namadi
Makinde ex-allies’ support strengthens Alli’s bid – Oyo APC campaign

headline: All Progressives Congress Intensifies Preparations For 2027 Election
metaDescription: The All Progressives Congress begins campaign activities for 2027 in Jigawa and Oyo states while announcing plans for the Kaduna-Kano rail project.
aiSummaryBullets: The All Progressives Congress inaugurated its 2027 campaign council in Jigawa state to support President Bola Tinubu and Governor Namadi.
In Oyo state, the party candidate Sharafadeen Alli is building support through a realignment of political figures formerly allied with the governor.
The party stated that the Kaduna-Kano railway line is scheduled for official inauguration on December 3.
aiContextParagraph: The All Progressives Congress is mobilizing ahead of the 2027 general elections across several Nigerian states. In Jigawa, party leaders have established a formal campaign structure to unify support for President Bola Tinubu and Governor Namadi. Meanwhile, in Oyo state, gubernatorial candidate Sharafadeen Alli is working to leverage shifting political allegiances among former allies of the current administration to strengthen his campaign position. Separately, the party has highlighted infrastructure developments, specifically noting that the Kaduna-Kano railway project is set for inauguration on December 3. Reports indicate that the status of this rail project has evolved significantly since the current presidential administration took office in 2023, when construction progress for the line was reported to be below 30 per cent. These collective developments represent ongoing strategic efforts by the ruling party to align political machinery and showcase national project milestones as the next election cycle approaches.
whyItIsViral: This story is trending due to coordinated political activities from the ruling party, captured by multiple national outlets reporting on campaign inaugurations and infrastructure updates.
